discovery_and_framing.subtitle: Establish current funnel and baseline before proposing solutions

lesson.hook: Stop pitching features before you even know where the bucket leaks.
lesson.what: Discovery and framing means defining the exact retention baseline and current funnel bottlenecks before proposing any levers. You must quantify the current state of user drop-off before touching product solutions.
how: Map the exact user journey steps.
Identify the specific drop-off metric baseline.
State the quantitative business goal clearly.
lesson.example: For our personal finance app, day thirty retention sits at eight percent after users check net worth once. We need to lift that baseline to fifteen percent.
lesson.mistake: Jumping straight into building new gamification features without establishing the current leaky funnel metrics.

questions.caseTitle: Reduce churn in a language learning platform.
questions.scenario: Users download our language app, complete three lessons, and vanish by day seven.
questions.question: How should you frame this retention problem at the start of your answer?
options: Introduce social leaderboards so friends can compete on daily lesson streaks.
Propose adding daily push notifications to remind users to complete lessons.
Redesign the onboarding tutorial flow to make learning languages much easier.
State our current day thirty baseline and target twenty percent retention.
questions.explanation: Establishing the current baseline and target metric is the core of discovery and framing. Proposing features too early skips this essential diagnostic step.
whyWrong: This adds engagement features before diagnosing the retention leak.
This proposes a solution lever before defining the baseline metrics.
This jumps straight to a redesign without analyzing funnel drop-offs.

questions.caseTitle: Improve retention for a personal finance app.
questions.scenario: People download our finance app, connect bank accounts, look at net worth once, and vanish.
questions.question: What is the best way to open your case response using good framing?
options: Gently nudge users to check their accounts every single morning at breakfast.
Note our grim eight percent day thirty retention baseline and define the goal.
Build a weekly spending summary email digest to drive daily engagement loops.
Add budgeting widgets to the home screen for quick financial tracking access.
questions.explanation: Good framing requires explicitly stating the current baseline metric and target before discussing solutions. The other options introduce premature product levers.
whyWrong: This assumes a tactical solution without first diagnosing the core leak.
This jumps into an engagement feature before establishing the retention baseline.
This suggests a product widget before quantifying the funnel drop-off.

questions.caseTitle: How would you grow Netflix's user base in Southeast Asia?
questions.scenario: Acquisition is stalling in Indonesia and the Philippines due to pricing and payment drop-offs.
questions.question: How should you structure the initial discovery phase of your answer?
options: Run localized marketing campaigns highlighting popular regional drama series.
Suggest launching lower priced mobile tiers for price sensitive regional users.
Highlight healthy brand awareness but massive payment screen drop-offs first.
Partner with local telecom carriers to bundle subscriptions into data plans.
questions.explanation: Mapping where the funnel stalls before proposing acquisition tactics demonstrates strong discovery skills. Jumping to telecom partnerships bypasses the funnel analysis.
whyWrong: This jumps to marketing tactics before diagnosing the payment screen leak.
This proposes a pricing lever before analyzing the funnel bottlenecks.
This suggests a distribution channel partnership without framing the drop-off.

questions.caseTitle: Prioritize Growth vs Retention at Uber Eats
questions.scenario: We are burning engineering hours chasing new restaurants while day thirty user retention is dismal.
questions.question: What should be your very first move when answering this case?
options: Redesign the restaurant discovery feed to highlight popular local food spots.
Pinpoint our fifteen percent thirty day user retention as a leaky bucket.
Slow down restaurant acquisition efforts entirely to focus on push notifications.
Offer free delivery promotions to incentivize customers to place repeat orders.
questions.explanation: Framing the leaky bucket by stating the poor retention baseline establishes the core problem. The other choices immediately suggest solutions without framing.
whyWrong: This suggests a UI redesign before establishing the funnel metrics.
This prescribes a tactical shift without framing the underlying retention baseline.
This proposes a promotional lever before defining the retention problem.

questions.caseTitle: Increase daily active creators on TikTok.

questions.question: How should you frame the core problem during your opening statement?
options: Build simplified editing templates to help creators produce videos faster.
Add cash incentives for creators who publish videos three times weekly.
Define our goal to increase daily active creators by ten percent soon.
Launch a creator mentorship program to guide new users through filming.
questions.explanation: Establishing a clear target goal and identifying the active creator gap is proper framing. The other options jump straight into feature proposals.
whyWrong: This proposes a product feature before establishing the creator funnel baseline.
This suggests a financial incentive lever without defining the core metric goal.
This jumps to an operational program before analyzing the creator drop-off.

questions.caseTitle: Increase merchant retention on Amazon Marketplace.

Lower seller subscription fees across all categories to improve merchant margins.
Create an educational webinar series explaining how to optimize product listings.
Lift ninety day retention for new merchants listing few items from twenty percent.
questions.explanation: Quantifying the specific ninety-day merchant retention baseline and target demonstrates rigorous funnel discovery. The other options propose specific levers too early.
whyWrong: This proposes a marketing lever before analyzing the merchant drop-off funnel.
This suggests a pricing change before framing the merchant retention baseline.
This jumps to an educational initiative without establishing the current metrics.

Integrate video conferencing directly into channels for easier team communication.
Establish our team active threshold baseline and target weekly retention rate.
Send automated email reminders to team administrators about unread messages.
questions.explanation: Defining the activity threshold and retention baseline correctly frames the problem before solutioning. All other options pitch features prematurely.
whyWrong: This jumps to a user interface redesign without framing the funnel leak.
This suggests building a new feature before analyzing the team drop-off.
This proposes a notification tactic before establishing the retention baseline.

options: Assign a dedicated account manager to help every single new property owner.
Guarantee host earnings for their first month to remove financial listing fears.
Map our host onboarding funnel and quantify the drop-off at photo upload.
Simplify the property description form fields to reduce typing friction.

whyWrong: This suggests an operational staffing solution without framing the metrics.
This proposes a financial incentive before analyzing the onboarding funnel drops.
This jumps to a form redesign before quantifying the exact activation leak.

funnel_or_loop.subtitle: Master the art of diagnosing leaky funnels and compounding growth loops

lesson.hook: Stop guessing why users leave. Master the math of leaks and loops instead.
lesson.what: A growth model maps every conversion stage from acquisition to retention. It exposes exact drop-off points and compounding loops.
lesson.example: For Spotify, you map casual weekly listeners into daily habit loops by analyzing mid-week listening drops.
lesson.mistake: Focusing on top-of-funnel acquisition while ignoring massive retention leaks.

questions.caseTitle: Reduce churn in a language learning platform.
questions.scenario: Users download the language app, complete three lessons quickly, and then vanish entirely by day seven.
questions.question: What is the primary funnel metric to target first for maximum compounding impact?
options: Lift day thirty retention baseline
Increase total app store downloads
Lower initial content creation costs
Boost total lifetime ad revenue
questions.explanation: Targeting early habit formation directly fixes the day seven drop-off leak. This improves long-term retention before spending more on top-of-funnel acquisition.
whyWrong: Driving more downloads just fills a leaky bucket with more churning users.
Reducing content costs has zero direct impact on user habit formation or early retention.
A smart candidate might focus on monetization, but revenue follows engagement and retention.

questions.caseTitle: How would you grow Netflix's user base in Southeast Asia?
questions.scenario: Brand awareness is high in Indonesia and the Philippines, but potential subscribers abandon the signup flow at the payment screen.
questions.question: Where is the core funnel leak requiring immediate strategic intervention?
options: Initial social media brand awareness
The content recommendation algorithm
The pricing and payment screen
Customer service response times
questions.explanation: Users drop off at the payment screen due to monthly pricing friction in mobile-first markets. Fixing this localized payment barrier unlocks the acquisition funnel.
whyWrong: Brand awareness is already strong, so spending effort there misses the actual drop-off point.
Recommendation algorithms affect retention later, not the initial payment screen drop-off.
Customer service happens post-purchase and does not cause pre-payment drop-offs.

questions.caseTitle: Increase daily active creators on TikTok.
questions.scenario: TikTok has one billion monthly users, but only ten percent create content regularly while the rest just watch.
questions.question: What core funnel bottleneck must be addressed to increase active creators?
options: The slow video upload speed
The blank page creation terror
The lack of music track options
The complex app store download
questions.explanation: Creators drop off before filming because they face intimidation when staring at a blank screen. Removing this friction increases the volume of active creators.
whyWrong: Upload speed is rarely the main reason people hesitate to start filming videos.
Music options are abundant, so lack of tracks is not the primary creation blocker.
App store downloads happen before someone even thinks about creating content.

questions.caseTitle: Improve onboarding for first-time merchants on Stripe.
questions.scenario: First-time merchants abandon signups during KYC verification and technical configuration steps.
questions.question: How should you restructure the activation funnel to improve merchant retention?
options: Simplify compliance and technical jargon
Redesign the entire public website
Offer massive transaction fee discounts
Increase outbound sales phone calls
questions.explanation: Merchants drop off because technical jargon and complex compliance overwhelm them. Simplifying these onboarding steps directly lifts early activation rates.
whyWrong: A public website redesign ignores the logged-in onboarding and compliance bottleneck.
Fee discounts eat into margins without solving the actual compliance confusion.
Outbound calls do not fix the self-serve technical configuration drop-off point.

questions.caseTitle: Increase repeat usage for a food delivery app.
questions.scenario: DoorDash loses sixty percent of new food delivery users after their first order due to high decision friction.
questions.question: What intervention best stabilizes the repeat usage loop for these new users?
options: Acquire more restaurants in new cities
Increase delivery radius significantly
Send generic push notifications daily
Curate personalized repeat order options
questions.explanation: First orders involve choice overload, so surfacing curated repeat options reduces friction. This drives users past the dangerous first-order drop-off cliff.
whyWrong: Acquiring new restaurants helps top-of-funnel but fails to fix existing user churn.
Expanding delivery radius hurts food quality and increases late delivery churn.
Generic daily push notifications annoy users and increase uninstalls instead of retention.

questions.caseTitle: Design a viral loop for Dropbox's file-sharing feature.
questions.scenario: Eighty percent of free signups drop off within thirty days because they run out of storage space.
questions.question: Which loop mechanic best converts free signups into active paying users?
options: Drive shared folder user adoption
Run expensive television advertising
Offer free storage for signing in
Provide unlimited files to everyone
questions.explanation: Users who share folders retain at twice the rate and convert faster. Driving shared folder adoption creates a viral loop that solves the storage drop-off.
whyWrong: Television ads acquire users but do not solve the underlying free-tier storage drop-off.
Giving free storage without sharing just delays the inevitable storage limit problem.
Providing unlimited free files destroys the monetization model and prevents upgrades.

questions.caseTitle: Slack Workspace Growth Loop
questions.scenario: New team members join Slack workspaces via invite links, but many send zero messages and go dormant.
questions.question: How do you optimize the activation funnel for newly invited team members?
options: Charge their company card immediately
Remove all channels except general
Prompt them with guided first tasks
Send weekly email digests to admins
questions.explanation: Guided first tasks reduce the intimidation of an empty workspace and drive activation. This turns invited signups into active weekly messaging participants.
whyWrong: Charging immediately causes instant churn before users experience any team value.
Removing channels destroys context and makes communication much less relevant.
Admin email digests do nothing to help the individual invited user send messages.

questions.caseTitle: Notion Template Sharing Loop
questions.scenario: Users browse community Notion templates, duplicate them into their workspace, but never create original pages.
questions.question: What is the key funnel transition needed to turn template copiers into creators?
options: Prompt custom edits within template
Force users to watch tutorials
Hide templates behind paywalls
Send promotional discount codes
questions.explanation: Prompting custom edits transforms passive template consumers into active creators. This bridges the gap between passive viewing and genuine workspace habit formation.
whyWrong: Forcing long video tutorials creates immense friction and drives users away.
Hiding templates behind paywalls kills the viral acquisition and duplication loop.
Discount codes do not solve the habit gap of actually building custom pages.

lever_identification.subtitle: Pinpoint the exact funnel leak with the biggest headroom.

lesson.hook: Stop fixing random metrics. Find the exact bottleneck that actually moves your business.
lesson.what: Lever identification means isolating the single step in your funnel with the highest drop-off and largest potential impact. Instead of guessing, you use baseline data to target where user behavior breaks down.
how: Map the user journey across every single key funnel stage.
Compare drop-off rates at each node against industry benchmarks.
Calculate potential impact and pick the lever with maximum headroom.
lesson.example: For Duolingo, instead of tweaking the home screen, you isolate day seven retention where casual users drop off.
lesson.mistake: The most common mistake is picking top of funnel acquisition when your actual leak is deep retention.

questions.caseTitle: Reduce churn in a language learning platform.
questions.scenario: Users download your language app, complete three quick lessons, and completely vanish by day seven.
questions.question: Which specific retention lever provides the greatest headroom for your product team right now?
options: Acquiring new users through expensive paid social media campaigns
Adding advanced grammar courses for power users who finish every module
Pushing day thirty retention from eight to twenty percent using early habits
Redesigning the settings page to reduce user support ticket volume
questions.explanation: Day seven churn is your biggest leak, and improving early habit formation unlocks massive long-term value. Fixing this specific drop-off protects all your acquisition efforts.
whyWrong: More acquisition just fills a leaky bucket faster without solving the core churn problem.
Advanced courses target power users, ignoring the early drop-offs where the real leak happens.
Support tickets are unrelated to the massive drop-off happening during the first week.

questions.caseTitle: Improve retention for a personal finance app.
questions.scenario: People download your finance app, link their bank accounts, check net worth once, and never return.
questions.question: What is the primary lever you should target to fix this early user drop-off?
options: Creating a daily habit loop without triggering severe financial anxiety
Building a referral program to bring in more curious new users
Adding cryptocurrency tracking features for younger tech savvy consumers
Lowering subscription prices to convert more free users to paid tiers
questions.explanation: Users vanish after one check because there is no sustainable habit loop. Solving this engagement drop without causing stress is the key leverage point.
whyWrong: Referrals amplify acquisition, but they will just churn immediately like the current cohort.
Crypto features appeal to a niche audience rather than solving the core onboarding drop-off.
Pricing adjustments do not solve the underlying lack of utility keeping users away.

questions.caseTitle: How would you grow Netflix's user base in Southeast Asia?
questions.scenario: Brand awareness is high in Indonesia, but removing free trials causes massive drop-offs at the payment screen.
questions.question: Where is the exact funnel leak that requires your immediate optimization focus?
options: The payment screen drop-off caused by high pricing and mobile friction
The top of funnel marketing spend across major urban digital channels
The content catalog depth for international movies and local television shows
The recommendation algorithm accuracy for users who finish watching a movie
questions.explanation: Users show strong intent by reaching the payment screen but drop off due to pricing and friction. Removing this barrier captures high-intent prospects.
whyWrong: Marketing spend is working fine because brand awareness and initial intent are already healthy.
Catalog depth does not address why people stall right when they hit the paywall.
Recommendation algorithms help with long-term retention, not the initial payment screen drop.

questions.caseTitle: Increase daily active creators on TikTok.
questions.scenario: TikTok has one billion monthly users, but only ten percent create content while the rest just watch.
questions.question: Which specific lever should you pull to increase your daily active creator metric?
options: Increasing global marketing campaigns to attract more passive viewers
Eliminating the blank page terror by simplifying initial video creation prompts
Redesigning the video playback interface to improve viewer engagement time
Negotiating exclusive music licensing deals for top tier verified creators
questions.explanation: The core problem is creator activation, specifically the fear of starting. Easing this creation friction unlocks a massive pool of latent creators.
whyWrong: More viewers will not solve the low creation ratio among your existing user base.
Viewer engagement metrics focus on consumption, completely ignoring the creator activation goal.
Music deals help top creators, but they do not help hesitant first-time creators start.

questions.caseTitle: Improve onboarding for first-time merchants on Stripe.
questions.scenario: Forty percent of signups drop off during KYC verification and webhook configuration due to complex jargon.
questions.question: What is the highest leverage action to improve merchant activation this quarter?
options: Updating the pricing tiers to offer better discounts for high volume transactions
Simplifying KYC verification and technical jargon to reduce signup drop-off
Adding more payment gateway integrations for international currencies and alternative wallets
Running aggressive digital advertising campaigns targeted at enterprise software companies
questions.explanation: The steep wall of compliance causes massive drop-off early on. Simplifying this onboarding flow is the fastest way to increase activation.
whyWrong: Pricing discounts do not help merchants who cannot even complete the initial setup.
New gateway integrations do not solve the immediate friction of identity verification.
Advertising brings in more merchants who will just hit the same compliance wall and churn.

questions.caseTitle: Boost Booking.com Repeat Bookings
questions.scenario: Booking frequency is down year over year, forcing you to work twice as hard on expensive paid search.
questions.question: Which customer segment and behavior should you target to restore repeat bookings?
options: Brand new users who find your platform through organic search engines
Business travelers who expense luxury hotel rooms every single week
Dormant accounts that have not opened your application in two years
Mobile app leisure travelers who book trips twice a year
questions.explanation: Targeting leisure app users addresses the specific frequency drop. Retaining existing travelers is cheaper than constantly buying new search traffic.
whyWrong: New users require expensive paid acquisition, which ignores the repeat booking problem.
Business travelers have completely different booking patterns and are not the core segment here.
Dormant accounts are too cold to efficiently convert into regular repeat bookers.

questions.caseTitle: Optimize Onboarding Flow for Notion Workspaces
questions.scenario: New teams create a Notion workspace, stare at a blank page, and abandon the tool within twenty minutes.
questions.question: What is the most effective lever to drive early team activation and retention?
options: Sending daily email reminders with marketing case studies and product updates
Redesigning the brand logo and marketing homepage to improve conversion rates
Providing interactive templates that guide teams to their first completed project
Increasing the file upload storage limits for all free tier workspace accounts
questions.explanation: Interactive templates remove the blank page terror, helping teams experience core value quickly. This direct guidance drastically improves early activation.
whyWrong: Daily emails are often ignored or marked as spam without delivering immediate product utility.
Homepage redesigns fix top-of-funnel acquisition, not the in-app workspace abandonment issue.
Storage limits do not help teams who cannot figure out how to start writing anything.

questions.caseTitle: Scale Creator Monetization on Substack
questions.scenario: Writers publish free newsletters on Substack, but struggle to convert free readers into paid subscribers.
questions.question: Which lever should you optimize to maximize paid subscription conversion rates?
options: Making it seamless for writers to gate specific paragraphs behind a paywall
Adding more social media sharing buttons to the bottom of every newsletter
Building automated recommendation widgets that feature competing newsletter publications
Lowering the platform fee percentage taken from established multi-author publications
questions.explanation: The conversion leak happens when writers cannot easily create compelling paywalls. Streamlining this feature directly drives paid subscription growth.
whyWrong: Sharing buttons help with reach, but they do not directly convert free readers into payers.
Recommending competing newsletters might distract readers rather than converting them to paid.
Platform fees affect retention of top writers, not the conversion rate of free readers.

retention_insight.subtitle: Master retention curves, activation moments, and habit loops

lesson.hook: Stop pouring water into a leaky bucket and fix your retention leaks.
lesson.what: Retention insight is about understanding how users form lasting habits with your product. You must identify the critical activation moment that turns casual users into daily regulars.
how: Find the exact day where retention flatlines.
Identify the core action that predicts long term usage.
Design a lightweight daily habit loop to prevent churn.
lesson.example: At Duolingo, users who complete three lessons by day seven form a lasting daily habit.
lesson.mistake: Focusing too much on top of funnel acquisition while ignoring immediate user churn.

questions.caseTitle: Reduce churn in a language learning platform.
questions.scenario: Your language app has strong downloads but users vanish completely by day seven.
questions.question: What is the most critical metric to analyze first in this retention leak?
options: Evaluate the total revenue generated from premium subscription upgrade conversions.
Measure total app downloads across all global marketing acquisition channels.
Calculate the daily cost per click for paid user acquisition campaigns.
Track thirty day retention baseline to measure early habit formation success.
questions.explanation: Thirty day retention baseline reveals the exact magnitude of early user churn. Focusing here helps you build better habit loops before scaling acquisition.
whyWrong: Upgrade conversions matter later but do not explain why users vanish early.
Total downloads only show top of funnel volume and ignore post install dropoffs.
Cost per click measures acquisition efficiency rather than product retention health.

questions.caseTitle: Improve retention for a personal finance app.
questions.scenario: Users connect their bank accounts, view net worth once, and leave forever.
questions.question: Why does a standard daily financial check fail to create a retention loop?
options: Users prefer to manually log their monthly expenses inside physical spreadsheets.
The app lacks enough engaging multiplayer games to keep users returning daily.
Checking bank balances daily creates financial anxiety rather than positive engagement.
Modern banking APIs are too slow to refresh user balances every single day.
questions.explanation: Forcing users to inspect checking accounts triggers stress and avoidance. Successful finance apps must provide value without causing monetary anxiety.
whyWrong: Manual spreadsheets represent the exact friction that modern apps aim to eliminate.
Multiplayer games are irrelevant to personal finance utility and habit formation.
API speed is rarely the primary driver of voluntary user dropoff behavior.

questions.caseTitle: Google Search App Engagement Retention
questions.scenario: Users download the search app for quick queries and leave without returning.
questions.question: What causes the sharp drop in user retention between day one and seven?
options: Marketing campaigns target the wrong demographic segments during launch phases.
The mobile application crashes whenever users search for flight status details.
Users complete transactional queries and leave without forming a habit loop.
Competitor search engines offer significantly faster web page loading speeds.
questions.explanation: Single use transactional queries solve an immediate need without establishing a habit loop. Users get their answer and have no reason to reopen the app.
whyWrong: Targeting demographics affects initial acquisition quality more than post query retention.
App crashes would cause immediate same day abandonment rather than gradual week one dropoff.
Loading speed differences are minor compared to the fundamental lack of habit utility.

questions.caseTitle: Prioritize Growth vs Retention at Uber Eats
questions.scenario: New restaurant acquisition is booming, but thirty day user retention sits at fifteen percent.
questions.question: How should the product team reallocate resources to fix this leaky bucket?
options: Redesign the entire restaurant dashboard to improve merchant onboarding speeds.
Lower delivery fees across all tier three cities to boost order volume.
Pause top of funnel acquisition to build early ordering habit loops.
Increase marketing budgets to attract even more new restaurant customers.
questions.explanation: Pouring traffic into a leaky bucket wastes marketing budget. Fixing the habit loop ensures acquired users actually stick around for the long term.
whyWrong: Merchant dashboards help supply, but the scenario specifically highlights user retention.
Lowering fees subsidizes bad unit economics without solving the underlying retention leak.
Increasing marketing budgets accelerates churn by acquiring users who quickly leave.

questions.caseTitle: Increase daily active creators on TikTok.
questions.scenario: Only ten percent of monthly users create content while the rest only watch.
questions.question: What is the primary psychological barrier preventing casual viewers from creating content?
options: Creators refuse to post videos unless they receive guaranteed monetary compensation.
The algorithm suppresses new creator content to protect established influencers.
Blank page terror makes filming feel overwhelming and intimidating to users.
The video editing tools are too complex for average smartphone owners.
questions.explanation: Blank page terror paralyzes potential creators who open the app with good intentions. Removing friction in content creation helps activate passive viewers.
whyWrong: Monetary compensation is not the primary driver for casual short form video creation.
Algorithm suppression affects distribution rather than the initial urge to record.
Modern editing tools are heavily simplified, meaning creation fear is psychological.

questions.caseTitle: Reduce early churn for LinkedIn Premium subscribers.
questions.scenario: Users purchase subscriptions for specific job searches and cancel immediately afterward.
questions.question: Why do subscribers churn right after their initial trial or paid month ends?
options: Competitor professional networks offer free lifetime access to all recruiter tools.
The platform fails to process monthly credit card payments due to banking errors.
They achieve their immediate transactional goal and forget the ongoing subscription value.
Job seekers find permanent employment within forty eight hours of joining.
questions.explanation: Single use utility creates a cliff when the goal is reached. Subscriptions need continuous engagement loops beyond a single job search.
whyWrong: Free competitor networks lack the proprietary professional graph that LinkedIn provides.
Payment processing failures account for involuntary churn, not intentional cancellations.
Employment timelines vary greatly and rarely happen within forty eight hours.

questions.caseTitle: Notion Workspace Habit Formation
questions.scenario: New users create a blank workspace page and abandon it within ten minutes.
questions.question: What is the most effective onboarding strategy to drive long term workspace retention?
options: Send daily reminder emails listing all available advanced database features.
Force users to watch a thirty minute video tutorial before starting.
Require users to invite five colleagues before unlocking their personal workspace.
Provide prebuilt template galleries that solve immediate documentation problems.
questions.explanation: Templates eliminate blank page anxiety by giving users an immediate functional framework. This accelerates time to value and drives early activation.
whyWrong: Reminder emails about advanced features overwhelm beginners who need basic utility.
Long video tutorials introduce heavy friction and cause immediate user dropoffs.
Requiring colleague invites creates an impossible barrier before personal value is found.

questions.caseTitle: Slack Daily Team Communication
questions.scenario: Teams sign up for chat workspaces but stop messaging after the third day.
questions.question: Which specific activation threshold best predicts long term team retention in Slack?
options: Sending two thousand total messages across multiple custom channel categories.
Integrating third party developer tools like GitHub and Google Calendar.
Purchasing an annual enterprise subscription during the first week.
Uploading a custom team profile picture for every active member.
questions.explanation: Message volume is the core habit metric for communication tools. Teams that cross the threshold of two thousand messages are locked into the workflow.
whyWrong: Integrations are helpful but represent secondary habits compared to core messaging volume.
Enterprise purchases are financial milestones resulting from retention, not the cause.
Profile pictures are cosmetic and have zero correlation with team retention rates.

experiment_design.subtitle: Master experiment design with hypothesis, metrics, and sizing.

lesson.hook: Stop guessing what users want and start testing your brilliant product theories.
lesson.what: Experiment design means turning a guess into a structured test with clear metrics. It helps you measure true impact before writing massive code.
lesson.example: For Spotify, we hypothesize that adding a daily prompt will lift active streams by ten percent without raising crash rates. We will run a two week test on ten percent of free users.
lesson.mistake: Launching a massive feature test without defining a guardrail metric to catch hidden drops in core revenue.

questions.caseTitle: Reduce churn in a language learning platform.
questions.scenario: Users vanish by day seven after finishing only three quick lessons in our app.
questions.question: What is the best way to design an experiment for early habit formation here?
options: Redesign the entire app navigation to make lessons feel much faster.
Offer a fifty percent discount to all churned users immediately.
Send an email survey asking why they stopped using the product.
Test push reminders targeting day three to lift week one retention.
questions.explanation: Targeting day three directly attacks the exact leak point with a measurable loop. The other choices are too broad or rely on surveys.
whyWrong: A full redesign is too broad and impossible to measure cleanly.
Discounts destroy unit economics and fail to build sustainable daily habits.
Surveys capture opinions rather than driving actual behavioral changes.

questions.caseTitle: How would you grow Netflix's user base in Southeast Asia?
questions.scenario: Acquisition stalls at the payment screen in mobile first markets due to pricing friction.
questions.question: How should we structure an experiment to fix this payment drop off?
options: Increase monthly subscription prices to signal higher premium quality.
Run a massive television ad campaign across the entire region.
Add a localized mobile wallet option and measure checkout conversion.
Remove all payment steps completely and make the streaming service free.
questions.explanation: Adding a localized wallet directly targets the payment screen friction observed in the funnel. Free access or TV ads do not test payment fixes.
whyWrong: Higher prices will accelerate drop off at the payment screen rather than fixing it.
Television ads are top of funnel marketing, not product checkout optimization.
Making the service completely free destroys monetization and core business viability.

questions.caseTitle: Increase daily active creators on TikTok.
questions.scenario: Creators suffer from blank page terror and fail to publish videos after opening the app.
questions.question: Which experiment design best addresses the blank page terror for new creators?
options: Build a complex editing studio with professional desktop software tools.
Send push notifications telling creators to film viral dance trends.
Test AI video prompts and measure the percentage of users publishing.
Give cash prizes to the top ten creators with the most views.
questions.explanation: AI prompts directly target creation friction with a clear metric on publishing. Cash prizes or complex tools miss the core onboarding block.
whyWrong: Complex editing tools increase friction instead of solving blank page terror.
Push notifications are generic nudges that do not solve the root creation barrier.
Cash prizes reward existing creators rather than helping beginners overcome fear.

questions.caseTitle: Improve onboarding for first-time merchants on Stripe.
questions.scenario: Merchants drop off during KYC verification because technical jargon overwhelms them.
questions.question: How should we design a test to improve merchant activation during onboarding?
options: Send weekly email newsletters about advanced financial management tips.
Simplify compliance copy into plain terms and track seven day activation.
Remove all security compliance checks to make onboarding completely instant.
Require all merchants to schedule a phone call with sales reps.
questions.explanation: Simplifying copy addresses the jargon problem directly while tracking the right activation metric. Sales calls and removing compliance are flawed.
whyWrong: Newsletters do not solve the immediate KYC form drop off issue.
Removing compliance checks is illegal and ignores strict financial regulations.
Sales calls add massive friction and cannot scale for self serve merchants.

questions.caseTitle: Design a viral loop for Dropbox's file-sharing feature.
questions.scenario: Eighty percent of free signups drop off within thirty days because storage limits run out.
questions.question: What experiment structure best tests a referral habit loop for this product?
options: Charge users a monthly fee immediately after they sign up for an account.
Build a new chat messaging feature inside the file storage dashboard.
Make file sharing completely private by default to improve customer trust.
Offer extra storage space for every active friend invited and track conversion.
questions.explanation: Rewarding storage invites directly tackles the retention drop off by creating a natural viral loop. Private files or instant paywalls kill growth.
whyWrong: Charging immediately destroys top of funnel signups before they experience value.
A chat feature is a massive distraction from the core file sharing loop.
Making files private prevents sharing, which kills the core viral loop entirely.

questions.caseTitle: Increase repeat usage for a food delivery app.
questions.scenario: Sixty percent of new food delivery users churn after their first order due to choice overload.
questions.question: How should we design an experiment to lift repeat order rates here?
options: Test a curated reorder widget on the home screen for past items.
Send a daily customer satisfaction survey after every single meal delivered.
Double the delivery fees to increase company profit margins per order.
Hide all restaurant listings except for the single most expensive option.
questions.explanation: A curated reorder widget reduces choice overload and makes repeat ordering frictionless. Higher fees or hiding options will hurt retention.
whyWrong: Surveys measure satisfaction but do not solve the choice overload problem.
Doubling delivery fees will increase churn rather than driving repeat usage.
Hiding restaurants destroys variety and causes frustrated users to uninstall.

questions.caseTitle: Slack Workplace Habit Loop
questions.scenario: New teams adopt Slack but stop messaging after three days because communication stays in email.
questions.question: What is the most rigorous experiment design to drive team activation?
options: Send fifty automated notifications every hour to force users to reply.
Prompt teams to import an email thread and track week two message volume.
Remove all text chat features and replace them with video conference links.
Force users to invite ten external contractors before viewing any messages.
questions.explanation: Importing email threads brings existing habits into Slack and measures real message volume. The other options destroy user experience.
whyWrong: Spamming notifications will cause users to mute the app and uninstall.
Removing text chat completely ruins the core product value proposition.
Forcing external invites creates artificial friction that increases team churn.

questions.caseTitle: Notion Workspace Onboarding
questions.scenario: New users open Notion, see a blank page, and leave without creating any notes or pages.
questions.question: How should we test a solution to the blank canvas drop off problem?
options: Lock the account creation page until users buy an annual enterprise plan.
Require users to watch a one hour video tutorial before logging in.
Delete all default workspace features to keep the interface completely empty.
Preload templates based on user role and track thirty day active retention.
questions.explanation: Preloaded templates solve the blank page problem and let us measure long term retention. Locking pages or long videos create barriers.
whyWrong: Locking accounts behind enterprise plans will destroy signup conversion rates.
Long video tutorials cause severe drop off during the onboarding flow.
Deleting features leaves users with an even more intimidating blank screen.

scaling_plan.subtitle: Master what happens after your growth win and second-order effects.

lesson.hook: Winning feels great until your success breaks your infrastructure or kills your margins.
lesson.what: A scaling plan maps out how your solution handles massive volume increases. It also covers secondary system impacts.
how: Forecast infrastructure strain before opening up new channels.
Calculate unit economics at ten times current volume.
Identify negative second-order user behavior changes.
lesson.example: When scaling grocery delivery slots, we evaluated server load alongside driver burnout rates across peak rush hours.
lesson.mistake: Focusing only on initial conversion spikes while ignoring downstream support capacity.

questions.caseTitle: Reduce churn in a language learning platform.
questions.scenario: Your early habit loop intervention successfully pushed thirty day retention from eight percent to twenty percent.
questions.question: What critical second-order effect must you evaluate next regarding content consumption?
options: Server costs will drop because engaged users complete lessons faster.
Daily active users will decline because longer streaks create user fatigue.
Power users will exhaust our advanced curriculum much faster than expected.
Marketing teams can immediately cut all acquisition spend across social media.
questions.explanation: Users forming daily habits consume content at double the prior rate. You must scale production pipelines to prevent content exhaustion.
whyWrong: Server costs scale up with higher daily lesson completion rates.
Streak formation actually increases daily engagement rather than causing fatigue.
Retention gains do not replace the need for top of funnel acquisition.

questions.caseTitle: Improve retention for a personal finance app.
questions.scenario: Your daily habit loop for checking net worth is driving massive engagement but generating high notification volume.
questions.question: Which second-order scaling risk threatens long-term retention in this scenario?
options: Bank API connection fees will decrease due to bulk volume discounts.
Customer support headcount can be reduced by fifty percent immediately.
Engineering maintenance will drop because financial data rarely changes.
Users will experience notification fatigue and develop severe financial anxiety.
questions.explanation: Daily balance checks without positive framing trigger anxiety and app uninstalls. Scaling reminders requires careful personalization.
whyWrong: API provider costs scale linearly or per connection request.
Higher engagement generates more support inquiries about account syncing.
Financial integrations require constant maintenance due to bank security updates.

questions.caseTitle: How would you grow Netflix's user base in Southeast Asia?
questions.scenario: Localized pricing successfully drove massive subscriber acquisition across Indonesia and the Philippines.
questions.question: What primary infrastructure challenge must your scaling plan address immediately?
options: Mobile bandwidth limitations during peak evening streaming hours.
Excessive server capacity sitting idle during morning work hours.
Physical logistics delays for shipping physical media discs.
Customer acquisition costs rising because brand awareness is saturated.
questions.explanation: Massive subscriber growth on mobile networks strains regional peering and CDN bandwidth. Scaling requires optimizing bitrates for local infrastructure.
whyWrong: While usage patterns exist, peak load is the critical infrastructure threat.
Netflix operates entirely as a digital streaming service in these markets.
Acquisition costs were solved by localized pricing, not the core scaling bottleneck.

questions.caseTitle: Cross-Functional Retention Initiative at Netflix
questions.scenario: Your cross-functional retention push successfully lowered monthly churn between months two and three.
questions.question: How does this retention win impact the broader marketing and engineering ecosystem?
options: Engineering can deprecate all recommendation algorithms to save compute power.
Marketing can afford higher customer acquisition bids because lifetime value increased.
Product teams must stop building new features and focus entirely on billing.
Customer support tickets will increase because retained users are unhappy.
questions.explanation: Higher retention increases customer lifetime value. This allows growth marketing to bid more aggressively for new users.
whyWrong: Recommendation engines drive the retention that you just successfully achieved.
Product teams balance feature development alongside ongoing core optimization.
Retained users typically generate fewer urgent cancellation support tickets.

questions.caseTitle: Google Search App Engagement Retention
questions.scenario: Your new habit loop successfully converts transactional search queries into daily active utility habits.
questions.question: What is the primary second-order monetization risk of scaling this feature?
options: Users will perform fewer queries overall because answers are too direct.
Advertising revenue will automatically double without any additional engineering work.
Serving more complex intent queries increases compute costs per active user.
Query latency will improve because search indexes become much smaller.
questions.explanation: Handling complex intent queries at scale requires significantly more machine learning compute. You must factor this into unit economics.
whyWrong: Direct answers actually encourage higher search frequency among active users.
Ad revenue requires careful inventory management and auction scaling.
Search indexes grow larger and more complex as usage scales up.

questions.caseTitle: Design a referral strategy for a hyperlocal services app.
questions.scenario: Your referral program successfully creates high user density within targeted urban zip codes.
questions.question: What operational bottleneck will scaling this density cause for the supply side?
options: Platform commission rates must be reduced to zero for all partners.
Marketing teams will need to expand advertising into rural areas immediately.
Supply partners in those zip codes will face high utilization and burnout.
Service providers will experience idle travel time between remote jobs.
questions.explanation: High user density concentrates demand on local service providers. Without scaling supply, partners face burnout and churn.
whyWrong: Commission adjustments are pricing levers, not direct supply operational fixes.
Hyperlocal strategy focuses on density, not expanding into low density rural zones.
High density actually reduces travel time between jobs for service providers.

questions.caseTitle: Duolingo Daily Habit Formation
questions.scenario: Bonus Case: Your streak preservation feature successfully shifts casual users into daily learners.
questions.question: What second-order behavioral risk emerges when streak lengths grow very large?
options: Engagement automatically plateaus because users lose interest in learning languages.
Server costs decrease because long-term users require fewer daily API calls.
Users feel immense anxiety about breaking streaks and abandon the app entirely after a miss.
Monetization conversion rates increase because learners feel more confident.
questions.explanation: Extremely long streaks create high psychological pressure. When life interferes and a streak breaks, users often quit permanently.
whyWrong: Streak growth correlates with higher long-term retention and habit strength.
Daily active users generate consistent server load regardless of streak length.
Monetization is a business metric, not a behavioral risk of the streak itself.

questions.caseTitle: Spotify Listening Frequency
questions.scenario: Bonus Case: Your new algorithmic playlist feature successfully converts casual listeners into daily active users.
questions.question: What royalty and infrastructure constraint must your scaling plan address?
options: Streaming licensing costs scale linearly with consumption while subscription revenue is flat.
Server bandwidth requirements decrease because audio caching becomes completely free.
Artists will demand lower royalty payouts because their tracks get more total plays.
Music licensing fees drop significantly when user listening hours increase past a threshold.
questions.explanation: Music streaming operates on variable cost models where more listening directly increases royalty payouts. Scaling usage without premium conversion hurts margins.
whyWrong: Audio delivery bandwidth scales up linearly with total active listening hours.
Artist royalties are fixed contractual rates per stream across the platform.
Licensing fees generally scale per stream rather than offering volume discounts.
